indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive is kept, its S counting as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the boy is out, dismissed perhaps by being bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled' looks like the cricket dismissal, but it means put into a bowl, as greens are tossed in one. 'out' rearranges A LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of mixed leaves is typically served in a bowl, so it might be described as bowled.

clue.text: Loyal toast drunk in hock, presumably

explanation.surface: A patriotic toast to the monarch is raised by someone who has pawned everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hock' is slang for pawned; an article left with a pawnbroker is a security for the loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn toast drunk to someone's health is a vow of goodwill; a pawned article is security deposited against a loan.

parts.note: reads as a plain-looking or cosy physician, but points to the Victorian doctor who founded a famous chain of children's homes

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Barnardo was a 19th-century Irish-born physician who set up homes for destitute children in Britain; the charity still bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian philanthropist known as Dr Barnardo founded children's homes, making him the doctor of homes.

clue.text: Churchman gets a pass, yet goes astray

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the word yet wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is issued with a permit but still loses his way.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar server or assistant in church ritual is a minor church official.

clue.text: He may struggle to break a lock

definitions.text: He may struggle to break a lock

parts.words: He may struggle to break a lock
parts.note: reads as a burglar forcing a door lock, but the lock is a grappling hold in a bout on the mat

explanation.definitionFit: A grappler in a bout struggles to escape holds such as headlocks applied by an opponent.

clue.text: Scattered once and never to get together again

indicators.note: scattered means dispersed in all directions, so the letters of the two words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A group once dispersed and never to meet again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassemble a meeting or body after a break is to meet again.

clue.text: A number lead the union in time-wasting action

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so the number is placed before the union

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: A certain number lead the trade union in a go-slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union and 'action' industrial action, but the definition is idle trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle trifling or flirting is a frivolous way of passing time.
Inexperienced or fresh means raw and untried; the hue of grass is a colour.

clue.text: She gets the same bit of luck twice

indicators.note: twice means the same piece appears two times in a row
only a bit of the word luck is wanted, its first two letters, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A woman has the same stroke of fortune two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' keeps LU from luck (dropping CK) and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as she; also slang for a remarkable person.
As an adjective it means chief or principal; as a noun it is a senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church.

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters of push and to are reordered

explanation.surface: Perhaps a final shove brings matters to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or result of events is their conclusion.

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the strip

parts.note: a bar is a strip of metal or wood

indicators.note: leading means the letter at the front of the word entertainer

explanation.surface: A star performer headlines a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip show' reads as one phrase but splits: 'strip' gives BAR and 'show' is the definition, as a letter bears its signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or carry visibly, as a document bears a signature, is to exhibit it.

parts.note: true means correct or right
the letter O looks like zero, and love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A cheery exclamation of agreement addressed to a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a score of nothing is called love, so the round letter O can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved partner is a darling, the person one is devoted to.

parts.note: red is the colour of socialism, so it means left-wing

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the letters of Bert's and a are turned into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Robin is a leftie, and Bert is a firebrand too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin's' is read as 'Robin is', defining the bird's old name; 'left-wing' and 'revolutionary' suggest politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The European bird is traditionally called by this name for its orange-red chest feathers.

clue.text: Suit case found in the car

parts.note: gear is clothing, an outfit or suit
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A suitcase is discovered in the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit case' reads as luggage but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The transmission housing of a motor vehicle is a component under the bonnet.

clue.text: Rakes money in, in the usual ways

indicators.note: in places money within the rakes

parts.note: roués are rakes, dissolute men
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Dissolute men pocket cash by the usual methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular sequences of actions followed habitually are customary procedures.

indicators.note: outside means the short word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted outdoors to fetch fruit that was running low.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dried grape, or a soft berry such as blackcurrant, is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Naughty nun's feat is to unzip!

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters of nun's feat misbehave into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A mischievous nun's daring deed is to undo her zip.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a zip or other fastening is to undo it.
Many papers carry this title, such as the Chicago one; in ancient Rome it was an official championing the plebs, a popular leader.

indicators.note: rough means roughed up or disordered, so the letters of court and bad are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rough court deals with a wicked abductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries a person off by force is an abductor, a snatcher of people.

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing upwards, so the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.walkthrough: 'mounts' turns RE + IT upwards; 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A level of seating in a stadium or theatre is a line, one of several ranked one above another.

clue.text: Cigarettes there's still call for at some schools

definitions.text: there's still call for at some schools

explanation.walkthrough: At traditional English boarding schools a younger boy acted as a servant to an older one, a practice called fagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cigarettes; and junior boys who served seniors at English public schools, summoned by a call.

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-armed small primate is a type of ape; Edward, author of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, was the historian.

parts.note: reads as a fashion runway, but means the narrow back street where stray cats prowl, as in the term for a street cat

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow passage between buildings is the haunt of strays, hence the term for a street cat.
To befoul is to pollute or desecrate; a narrow gorge through mountains is a pass.

clue.text: It's played for the HQ dance

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Music is performed at the headquarters' dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' suggests music at a dance, but the definition is a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball game is a sport that people play.

clue.text: He splits a couple of poles made of wood

indicators.note: splits means the piece comes between, dividing the other letters

parts.note: S and N are the abbreviations for south and north, two poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man chops two poles to make something wooden.
explanation.definitionFit: Made from timber of the tree with winged seeds; also pale grey, the colour of cinders.

clue.text: Wrapped up in an unusually deep novel

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters of deep and novel are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in a strangely profound book.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered or encased completely, as in paper, is enclosed.
